header: Date: 2027-02-02T16:00Z | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Evan (Trident), Priya (Trident), Marcus (Trident), Aisha (Trident)
summary: Intro/demo of Redwood API and Console focused on migration from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. Showed parity mapping approach, console parity views, Optimize recommendations (batching/quantization), and Private vs Dedicated routing tradeoffs. Action items to share parity mapping spreadsheet and kick off a 24h performance run. Security + compliance pack requested.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run for ~45 minutes, quick intro then Sofia will do the parity mapping walkthrough and console demo. Evan: 00:05 Hi, looks good. We have Priya and Marcus on — thanks.
00:18 Sofia (Redwood SE): Great, hi all. Just to set expectations, this is a migration/showcase — we map your current OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood API equivalents and highlight differences, cost, and operational knobs.
00:35 Evan (Trident): Sounds good. main things for us: match latency, same output quality, and keep cost <= current baseline. Also, security — Marcus will ask questions.
00:50 Marcus (Trident): Yep. SOC 2 report, KMS integration, and audit logs are must-haves.
01:07 Jordan: We'll cover those; we also have a security pack to share. Okay Sofia?
01:15 Sofia: Cool — opening parity-mapping-trident.xlsx (link: parity-mapping-trident.xlsx). First column shows current calls: openai.ChatCompletion.create, anthropic.chat.create, together.generate. Next column maps to Redwood text-generation/chat endpoints and notes runtime parameters.
01:40 Priya: Quick question — Together models use different context handling. Does Redwood support the same long-context KV cache semantics?
01:48 Sofia: Good Q. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; we sometimes call it KV cache but downstream transcripts might show "KV cash" — ignore that. It handles variable-length cache and selective refill so you can keep state between calls. We also do automatic cache eviction based on LRU and sequence-length heuristics.
02:15 Liam (Redwood SE): For Together-style long contexts we recommend enabling continuous batching off on hot endpoints and using pinned KV shards in Dedicated for fastest hits.
02:30 Evan: What's the penalty if we switch to hosted vs Dedicated for those endpoints?
02:38 Sofia: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value — warm cache on common prefixes, but Dedicated gives predictable latency at scale and you can pin GPU types. We usually recommend a hybrid: Hosted for bursts and Dedicated for steady, critical endpoints.
02:58 Priya: Can Redwood do function/tool calling patterns like our current OpenAI calls? We rely on that heavily.
03:06 Sofia: Yes. Redwood supports function-style structured outputs and streaming. The only gotcha: if you rely on a specific tokenization behavior edge-case, we'll note that in parity mapping and give a compatibility shim in the SDK.
03:28 Marcus: On encryption — how does KMS work? Customer-managed keys?
03:34 Jordan: You can use Redwood Private with your KMS or when on Dedicated we can integrate customer-managed keys. Security pack includes diagrams.
03:45 Evan: Could you show the console bit? We want to see rollouts, metrics, and per-token cost breakdown.
03:52 Sofia: Sure — switching to Console. (keyboard noise) Console screenshot link: trident-console-preview.png. On the left is model catalog; you can pin a model version, create a rollout, and set fallback policies. The metrics pane shows token/latency/cost per route.
04:20 Sofia: Example: we set an A/B rollout 90/10 between a quantized variant and full FP model. Console shows the quality delta on a test prompt set and real-time regression alerts.
04:40 Evan: Nice — whats the usual quality hit on quantization? We saw mixed results moving from 8-bit to 4-bit.
04:50 Liam: It depends on model and prompt set. Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles by workload. For many instruction tuning cases, 8-bit gives negligible delta; for some long-context retrieval tasks 4-bit can produce hallucination spikes — Optimize flags those prompts.
05:18 Priya: Can we run those regressions against our golden prompt set?
05:23 Sofia: Yes — you upload an eval set in Console, we run A/B and show per-prompt diffs. We also store eval history so you can track regressions over time.
05:40 Evan: About cost — we currently pay per token to OpenAI; how does Redwood's per-token math compare?
05:48 Jordan: We'll share a modeled cost sheet. Short answer: you pay per-inference tokens but with caching and batching you can reduce units by 20-60% depending on workload. Redwood Optimize will suggest batch sizes and TTLs for prefix cache.
06:10 Marcus: Any remarks on data residency? We need EU-only for some endpoints.
06:16 Sofia: We support region pinning and Private VPC. You can run Private in your VPC or use Redwood Private deployed in a regional cloud with customer-managed network.
06:30 Aisha (Trident): Any changes needed in our infra to keep audit logs? We currently log all raw requests.
06:36 Jordan: You can stream audit logs to your SIEM, or fetch via API; Dedicated includes extended retention. We do not store plaintext for Private deployments unless you opt in.
06:50 Evan: Ok demo time — show a concrete mapping for one of our core endpoints.
06:57 Sofia: Example: your OpenAI chat calls with function-calling + system prompts map to Redwood's chat.create with functions array and role fields. (typing) Here's a snippet in the spreadsheet showing param differences — e.g., temperature vs top_p mapping, and for Together you often pass context differently, we normalize in the SDK shim.
07:30 Evan: Are there known tokenization differences that could change output length? We use token-based throttling downstream.
07:38 Liam: Some models and tokenizers differ; we include a tokenizer compat mode which maps incoming tokens and gives a delta estimate; it's in the parity sheet. It's approximate but helps you adjust rate limits.
07:57 Priya: For model fallback, like if a variant is OOM, can Redwood automatically fall back to another model? We need resilient behavior.
08:05 Sofia: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants, and you can set a fallback policy per route — immediate fallback, queue-and-retry, or degrade to cached response.
08:22 Evan: How about batching — our traffic has spiky bursts 300-500 rps. Does Redwood batching add latency?
08:30 Liam: Continuous batching is latency-aware: it will batch when it can within a max wait window. For SLO critical endpoints you can set batch-size=1 or prioritized lanes. For non-critical fan-out tasks batching reduces token cost dramatically.
08:52 Marcus: Can you show an example of the Optimize insights?
08:55 Sofia: Switching to Optimize module... (click) Optimize suggests: increase batch window to 50ms for this route, enable prefix caching on the retrieval route, and switch to quant-profile B for the embedder. It also flags 12 prompts with quality regression risk if you go to 4-bit.
09:22 Evan: We use embeddings a lot — latency matters. Any recommendation for embedding models and shard placement?
09:29 Liam: We often colocate embedder pools on Dedicated and pin them to smaller VMs with higher memory bandwidth; caching similar vectors helps too. For sparse retrieval, try RPC-level caching and bloom filters.
09:46 Aisha: Any limitations when migrating Together models that use custom sampling?
09:51 Sofia: If you've got custom samplers, SDK shims emulate behavior, but we'll enumerate differences in the parity mapping and include test vectors.
10:08 Evan: Alright, let's talk POC scoping. We want to run a 24-hour mirrored test of our top 5 endpoints with production traffic. What do you need from us?
10:18 Jordan: We need sample traffic, keys to replay or a synthetic generator, target SLOs, and list of golden prompts. Priya: we'll provide traffic profile.
10:26 Priya: We'll export a replay and a small sample within 48h.
10:30 Jordan: Great. We'll provision a Dedicated test pool or combination with Hosted. Sofia: We'll draft the perf-run checklist.
10:42 Evan: On pricing, if we need Dedicated capacity for the test, how's billing handled?
10:47 Jordan: For POC we typically offer credits or trial pricing; dedicated reserved pool has short term commit options for POC. We'll put details in the spreadsheet.
11:02 Marcus: Security: what about logging of prompt text? We need to redact PII.
11:08 Sofia: You control whether prompt text is stored in logs. For Private or Dedicated you can set no-retention or use customer-side redaction. We also support streaming encrypted logs to your S3.
11:22 Evan: What about canary rollouts for a model swap? We want an automated rollback on quality regression.
11:29 Liam: Console supports canary with auto-scale and regression-based rollback. You set an eval set and thresholds; if quality drops beyond X, system automatically rolls back and alerts the pipeline.
11:44 Priya: Any pitfalls moving from Anthropic in terms of safety filters or assistant-style prompts?
11:51 Sofia: Anthropic has different safety token heuristics; we recommend keeping an intermediate compatibility mode and running safety evals. Optimize will surface prompts that hit different safety gates.
12:08 Jordan: Quick note — prompts that rely on hidden Anthropic system policies might behave differently; parity mapping flags those and suggests prompt refactors.
12:21 Evan: Ok, can we get a quick demo of console creating a route and setting fallback?
12:26 Sofia: Sure — creating route 'trident-search': bind model 'redwood-oss-8b', set max latency 350ms, set fallback to 'redwood-oss-4b-quant' with immediate fallback. Now kicking a canary 10% to test.
12:48 Sofia: The dashboard shows request flow, percent served by primary, average latency 320ms, cache hit 18%. We can adjust batch window live.
13:05 Marcus: Those cache hit numbers, can we prewarm?
13:09 Liam: Yes, prewarming and persistent pinned KV shards in Dedicated boost hit rate. Also prefix-TTL tuning helps.
13:22 Evan: Let's talk observability — token-level cost attribution is important for our product lines.
13:29 Sofia: Console's per-route token breakdown shows per-request token consumption and cost estimate. You can attach tags for product lines and get cost trends.
13:40 Priya: We'll want RBAC for teams and SSO connection. How does Redwood integrate with our Okta?
13:47 Jordan: SSO via SAML/Okta supported. For Private/Dedicated, you can map roles and restrictions. We'll include recommended RBAC mappings.
14:05 Evan: Any non-obvious migration tasks?
14:09 Sofia: Tokenization deltas, function-calling schema differences, and any internal prompts that depend on specific sampling behaviours. Those are the top 3. We list them in parity mapping with mitigation steps.
14:26 Aisha: On incident management, who do we call at 3am?
14:30 Jordan: Dedicated customers can opt into 24/7 pager; Hosted has business-hours SLAs, but for enterprise we do 24/7. We'll include escalation contacts in the SOW.
14:47 Priya: For the 24h run — can we run in our VPC? We want to avoid egress.
14:53 Sofia: Yes for Private you can run in your VPC or we can deploy a Private control plane. For Dedicated, secure peering or PrivateLink can be set up.
15:07 Evan: Anything else on cost optimization?
15:11 Liam: Consider splitting inference patterns: short prompt generation on smaller quantized models, long context retrieval on Dedicated pinned pools. Also use prefix caching for repeated support prompts.
15:24 Marcus: Will you provide an estimate of cost delta for 12 months if we move core endpoints?
15:29 Jordan: Yes, we'll run a modeled projection and include caching and batching assumptions; sheet will show optimistic/pessimistic scenarios.
15:45 Priya: Regarding compliance, how do you handle audit logs retention? Can we set retention to 7 years?
15:51 Sofia: Dedicated/Private can support extended retention; Hosted has tiered retention windows. We'll include options in the security pack.
16:10 Evan: Okay, last piece — SDK changes. How intrusive is the change?
16:14 Liam: Most customers swap endpoints and minimal param remapping. We provide an SDK shim that translates a small set of calls. Function-calling payloads stay mostly the same. We'll provide an integration guide with diffs.
16:30 Jordan: Recap and next steps: we'll share parity spreadsheet, security pack, and the perf-run checklist. Trident to send traffic profile and golden prompts. We'll schedule POC kickoff.
16:44 Evan: That works — good session.
16:48 Jordan: Thanks all. Action items noted.
16:52 (end)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels and short ASR errors (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache", "TogetherAI" may be transcribed as "together a I"). Links shared during meeting: parity-mapping-trident.xlsx, trident-console-preview.png, security-pack.pdf.
